svg.title: The tool loop, with the permission gate on the only path to a server
svg.desc: A loop drawn as four stages left to right: connect and list, which builds the catalog and sends every name and description into the model's context; the model, which replies with text or with tool calls and arguments; the permission gate, which handles one call at a time so two prompts never race for the same terminal; and execute, where the approved calls reach servers. User text enters at the model. When the reply carries no tool calls the loop leaves immediately to a green box, the final answer, with a note that the branch is on the presence of tool calls and never on a provider stop-reason string. When it does carry tool calls they go to the gate, which has three exits. Allowed is the arrow that continues right into execute, and it is the only exit that reaches a server. Denied drops away to a red box saying the server is never called, and an unknown tool name drops to a grey box saying there is nothing to gate and the model should be told. All three, along with the results coming back out of execute, fall into one wide band: every requested call comes back with a result, in the order the model asked, in one turn, because a dropped result leaves a dangling tool-use identifier and results split across turns teach the model to stop asking for parallel calls. A return arc runs from that band up the right side and back over the top into the model, labelled as looping up to a maximum number of rounds. Two closing lines state that the gate has three exits and only one reaches a server, and that gating is sequential while execution is parallel.
svg.text: The tool loop, and the gate that sits in it
Gating is sequential. Execution is parallel. Every requested call comes back with a result, whether or not it ran.
branch on tool calls in the reply,
nothing to gate; tell the model
every requested call comes back with a result, in the order the model asked, in one turn
A dropped result leaves a dangling tool-use id. Splitting them across turns teaches the model to stop asking for parallel calls.
The gate has three exits and only one reaches a server. Denied calls and unknown names skip execution and still return a result.
Gating is sequential, one call at a time. Execution is parallel: gather the approved calls, then restore the model's order.
